\title{A Sharp Plaquette-Log Hessian Bound and a Finite Nonlinear Overlap Window}

\begin{abstract}
We sharpen the local nonlinear $SU(2)$ block certificate by computing the
exact identity Hessian of the plaquette logarithm.  Transporting this exact
value with the previously certified third derivative proves quotient
injectivity, fiber contraction, and generated-base coercivity throughout the
dependency-aware typical radius obtained from local Gaussian concentration.
This closes the finite local overlap gate, while normalized density comparison
and large-field charging remain open.
\end{abstract}

\section{Exact identity Hessian}
Let
\[
 F(A)=\log\bigl(e^{A_1}e^{A_2}e^{-A_3}e^{-A_4}\bigr),
 \qquad A_i\in\mathfrak{su}(2)\cong\mathbb R^3.
\]
The quadratic BCH term gives a bilinear Hessian
\[
 D^2F(0)[A,B]=\sum_{i,j=1}^4 C_{ij}A_i\times B_j,
\]
where, up to conjugation by a diagonal sign matrix,
\[
 C=\begin{pmatrix}
 0&1&1&1\\-1&0&1&1\\-1&-1&0&1\\-1&-1&-1&0
 \end{pmatrix}.
\]

\begin{theorem}
The bilinear operator norm of $D^2F(0)$ is
\[
 m_2(0)=\|C\|=1+\sqrt2.
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
In quaternion exponential coordinates $[A,B]=2A\times B$, so the one-half
in the quadratic BCH term cancels.  The singular values of $C$ are
$1+\sqrt2$ and $\sqrt2-1$, each twice.  Orthogonally reduce $C$ to two $2\times2$
symplectic blocks.  For one block,
\[
 \|A_1\times B_2-A_2\times B_1\|
 \le (\|A_1\|^2+\|A_2\|^2)^{1/2}
      (\|B_1\|^2+\|B_2\|^2)^{1/2}.
\]
Combining the two blocks by Cauchy--Schwarz gives the upper bound $\|C\|$;
singular vectors with orthogonal spatial directions attain it.
\end{proof}

If $M_3(r)$ is the certified third-derivative supremum on the joint
four-link ball, the mean-value theorem yields
\[
 \|D^2F(A)\|\le 1+\sqrt2+M_3(r)r=:m_2(r),
 \qquad
 \|DF(A)-DF(0)\|\le m_2(r)r.
\]
This replaces the former global Banach-log second-derivative majorant.

\section{Overlap certificate}
At heat time $t=3\cdot10^{-6}$, the local Gaussian theorem requires
\[
 r_{\rm typ}=0.006023157807602598.
\]
Substitution into the quotient Hessian and Schur-complement bounds gives:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lr}
\toprule
Quantity & certified value\\
\midrule
$m_2(r_{\rm typ})$ & $2.7110277092$\\
global derivative deviation & $0.0399975899$\\
nonlinear physical singular floor & $1.3742159724$\\
total Hessian remainder & $0.4746710866$\\
fiber margin & $1.5253289134$\\
generated-base margin & $0.6888073894$\\
centered fiber transport & $0.0619725685$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

All three local gates are strict.  The old certificate stopped at radius
$0.0042299674$; the sharp certificate remains valid to approximately
$0.0114537860$, an overlap factor $1.9016$ above the required radius.

\section{Frontier}
The theorem proves compatibility of local typical coverage and nonlinear
fiber/base control at one finite regulated scale.  It does not yet control the
normalizing partition-function ratio after arbitrary retained boundary data,
nor does it charge center, continuous, orbit, or topological complement
channels.  Those two estimates are the next nonperturbative target.  No RG,
continuum, or Hamiltonian mass-gap conclusion is asserted.
